title: Quentin and the Tide
premise: Wren Crane returns to Salt Hollow Point to run the family lighthouse after her grandmother's death, hiding her stalled writing career and her broken engagement behind a practiced smile. When her ex shows up at the reunion with a new fiancée, Wren recruits Quentin Marsh — a visiting maritime lawyer investigating the suspicious sale of the lighthouse land — to pose as her boyfriend. Their fake romance deepens into something real just as Quentin uncovers that Wren's own uncle orchestrated the land grab, forcing Wren to choose between protecting her family's fragile peace and pursuing justice outside the law. In the end, Wren testifies at the county hearing, the lighthouse is saved and deeded to her, and she chooses Quentin — writing their story as her first honest novel.
about_author: Juniper Fairweather is the pen name of a former tide-pool docent who spent ten years cataloging sea glass along the Pacific coast before turning to fiction. She writes love stories set in coastal towns where the weather always has an opinion.

chapters.title: The Light Keeps Its Own Hours
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren arrives at Salt Hollow Point to settle her grandmother's estate, cataloging the lighthouse keeper's logbooks and her own unfinished novel. She tells herself she's only staying a month. Emotional beat: grief disguised as efficiency, the ache of returning to a place that remembers who you were.

chapters.title: Reunion Weather
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Crane family reunion looms, and Aunt Dolores has already asked about Wren's ex-fiancé, Marcus, twice on the phone. Wren drafts a lie and hates how easily it comes. Emotional beat: dread, the performance of being fine.

chapters.title: A Man Reading Tide Tables
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin Marsh checks into the Salt Hollow Inn, ostensibly on vacation, actually following a paper trail on the Meridian Bay Development Group's purchase of coastal parcels. He notices the lighthouse keeper's granddaughter arguing with a surveyor. Emotional beat: wary curiosity, a professional instinct he can't switch off.

chapters.title: Coffee, Black, and a Bad Idea
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren meets Quentin at the Driftwood Café while eavesdropping on his phone call about 'parcel 47' — her parcel. They trade guarded small talk; she finds him annoyingly perceptive. Emotional beat: spark under suspicion.

chapters.title: The Terms of the Arrangement
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Desperate after Dolores announces Marcus is attending the reunion, Wren proposes a fake-dating deal to Quentin: one weekend, no questions. He agrees, oddly fast. Emotional beat: bargain struck, both hiding real motives.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Lie
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. They invent a meet-cute over chowder at the inn, and Quentin is startled by how easily Wren laughs with him — and how little he wants the weekend to end. Emotional beat: the fake becoming comfortable too quickly.

chapters.title: The Crane Reunion, Act One
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The reunion begins: cousins, casseroles, and Marcus arriving with his new fiancée, Priya, who is genuinely lovely. Wren introduces Quentin with a steadiness she doesn't feel. Emotional beat: humiliation deflected by performance.

chapters.title: Dessert and the First Crack
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. By dessert, Quentin has charmed Dolores and caught Marcus needling Wren in the kitchen. He steps in, hand at her back, and the touch lands like something real. Emotional beat: the lie tipping over into truth.

chapters.title: Moonwalk on the Breakwater
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Escaping the party, Wren and Quentin walk the breakwater under a full moon and tell each other almost-true things — her abandoned novel, his dead brother. Emotional beat: intimacy by way of omission.

chapters.title: Parcel Forty-Seven
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin confirms the lighthouse parcel is the keystone of Meridian Bay's marina project, and the signature on the sale option belongs to Wren's uncle Ray. He says nothing to her. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into secrecy.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Logbook
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Reading her grandmother's logbooks, Wren finds a 1998 entry about Ray and a land deal gone wrong — a debt, a signature, a silence. She begins to wonder what the lighthouse actually costs to keep. Emotional beat: inheritance as mystery.

chapters.title: One More Weekend
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The fake-dating deal was for one weekend; Quentin asks, casually, if it could extend. Wren says yes before she can think. Emotional beat: want outrunning caution.

chapters.title: Storm Watch
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A coastal storm knocks out power, and the two keep the lighthouse lamp running the old way. Working side by side, they stop pretending this is rehearsal. Emotional beat: closeness forged in emergency.

chapters.title: What Marcus Saw
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Marcus catches Wren and Quentin kissing on the gallery deck and, to her shock, looks less jealous than afraid — and warns her to 'ask Ray about the marina.' Emotional beat: the past tense cracking open.

chapters.title: Uncle Ray's Version
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts Ray, who admits he signed the option years ago to cover a debt but claims Meridian forged the renewal. He begs her not to fight it. Emotional beat: loyalty at war with justice.

chapters.title: The File Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin finds Meridian's forged renewal documents and a payoff ledger — and realizes his old firm, Hale & Croft, represented Meridian. He once billed hours on this very file. Emotional beat: complicity discovered in oneself.

chapters.title: Two Liars at Breakfast
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Over breakfast, Wren admits she knows about parcel 47; Quentin admits he knew first and hid it. The fight is quiet and devastating. Emotional beat: trust fractured by parallel secrecy.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Back
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin walks the coast alone, drafting and discarding an apology, understanding that he came to Salt Hollow to atone for Hale & Croft and instead repeated the pattern. Emotional beat: reckoning with himself.

chapters.title: Priya Calls It
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Priya, sharp and kind, tells Wren she saw the kiss and that Marcus is scared because he consulted for Meridian too. She offers to testify if it comes to that. Emotional beat: unlikely sisterhood.

chapters.title: The Hearing Notice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The county posts notice of a public hearing on the marina permit — in three weeks. Ray begs Wren to stay silent for family peace; Dolores sides with Ray. Emotional beat: the cost of speaking made concrete.

chapters.title: What the Novel Was For
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren rereads her abandoned manuscript and realizes she stopped writing when she stopped telling the truth. She starts a new page: the story of the lighthouse, the forgery, the fake date that wasn't. Emotional beat: voice recovered.

chapters.title: Quentin's Confession
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin tells Wren everything — Hale & Croft, the billable hours, his brother's drowning in a cove Meridian's first project destroyed, the real reason he's here. Emotional beat: shame offered without armor.

chapters.title: Not Forgiveness, Not Yet
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren doesn't forgive him, but she doesn't send him away; she hands him the keeper's logbook and says they build the case together or not at all. Emotional beat: trust rebuilt as a working agreement.

chapters.title: The Archive Run
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin and Wren drive to the county archive and pull the original option, notarization records, and a 1999 complaint her grandmother filed and then withdrew. Emotional beat: the grandmother's hidden fight discovered.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Withdrawal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A retired notary reveals Gran withdrew her complaint after Ray's daughter got sick and the family needed Ray's insurance. Wren understands the silence was love, and that love can still be wrong. Emotional beat: grief complicated by understanding.

chapters.title: Pressure from the Peninsula
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Meridian's lawyers — Quentin's old mentor among them — offer Wren a buyout with a confidentiality clause, and threaten to expose Quentin's conflict of interest if he testifies. Emotional beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: The Buyout Dinner
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At a tense dinner, Wren declines the buyout publicly, and Dolores walks out calling her a traitor to the family. Quentin is barred from the hearing by an ethics complaint. Emotional beat: isolation as the price of the choice.

chapters.title: Alone with the Lamp
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren keeps the light through a fog bank alone and confronts the possibility of losing everything: the lighthouse, the family, Quentin. She writes the hearing testimony by lamplight. Emotional beat: the dark before the decision.

chapters.title: Quentin's Gambit
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin drives to the state capital and files a whistleblower disclosure with the bar and the attorney general, torching his career to make his testimony admissible. Emotional beat: sacrifice as proof.

chapters.title: Ray Breaks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Shown the whistleblower filing and his granddaughter's testimony draft, Ray collapses and agrees to testify about the forged renewal. Emotional beat: a coward choosing, late, to be brave.

chapters.title: The Eve of the Hearing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The night before, Quentin returns uninvited. They don't resolve everything; they agree that whatever happens tomorrow, the fake date was the truest thing either of them has done. Emotional beat: love stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: The Hearing, Part One
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren testifies, voice shaking, laying out the forgery and the family history. Meridian's counsel tries to paint her as a jilted novelist with a grudge. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into testimony.

chapters.title: The Hearing, Part Two
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin testifies despite the ethics cloud, presenting the ledger and his own firm's complicity. The room turns. His mentor looks away. Emotional beat: justice costing exactly what it's worth.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The county denies the marina permit and refers the forgery to the district attorney. Dolores, present in the back row, doesn't applaud — but she doesn't leave. Emotional beat: victory that feels like an exhale, not a trumpet.

chapters.title: What Ray Gave Back
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ray signs the lighthouse and parcel 47 over to Wren outright, a partial amends. Dolores comes by with a casserole and an apology that isn't one, which is how her family says sorry. Emotional beat: imperfect reconciliation.

chapters.title: The Bar's Answer
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The bar declines to disbar Quentin; his whistleblower filing earns a quiet commendation and the end of his corporate career. He's free and unemployable and oddly light. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt from loss.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finishes the novel — their story, names changed badly — and reads the last page aloud to Quentin on the gallery deck. Emotional beat: art and love arriving as the same act.

chapters.title: First Real Date
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. Their first official, non-fake date: chowder at the Driftwood Café, the same booth, nothing pretended. Marcus sends a card; Priya signs it too. Emotional beat: joy without an audience for the first time.

chapters.title: Lighting the Lamp Together
chapters.summary: Both POVs converging. One year later: Wren's novel is under contract, Quentin works coastal land disputes for the community trust, and they light the lamp together for the season's first dark. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, kept, and lit.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The Tide Turns Anyway
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, journal entries from the keeper's logbook, hers now. She records the year's tides, the DA's conviction of Meridian's fixer, and Quentin asleep in the keeper's chair. Final line: the light keeps its own hours, and so do the people who stay. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled — not land, but the keeping.
